content.title: McDonald’s releasing South Korean-inspired 'KPop Demon Hunters' meals
content.text: Updated March 31, 2026, 9:18 a.m. MTMcDonald's is having a moment, and it's golden.Inspired by "KPop Demon Hunters," winner of two Oscars in 2026, the global fast-food giant is set to release two new meals themed after girl group HUNTR/X and their rivals, the Saja Boys, on March 31.Each meal lets fans choose a side and comes with a collectible card pack featuring an exclusive photocard from that group, along with a Derpy access card — named after a tiger character in the film. Guests can scan the card’s QR code and enter it in the McDonald’s app by April 26 to unlock exclusive content and a special reveal of the group that wins the ‘Battle for the Fans.’”When it comes to what’s inside, the meals pull inspiration from McDonald’s restaurants in South Korea, “connecting fans to the film through taste,” according to the March 24 news release.A look inside McDonald’s “KPop Demon Hunters” mealsMcDonald’s will offer two themed meals tied to rival groups in the film — the HUNTR/X Meal and the Saja Boys Breakfast Meal — each built around its own lineup of flavors and sauces. The meals launch March 31.The HUNTR/X MealThe HUNTR/X Meal is a classic 10-piece Chicken McNuggets meal paired with a medium soft drink, plus three limited-time menu items:Ramyeon McShaker Fries — an umami take on classic McDonald’s fries, seasoned with soy, garlic, sesame and spice.Hunter Sauce — a sweet chili dipping sauce.Demon Sauce — a spicy, tangy mustard-based sauce.Saja Boys Breakfast MealFor those who want breakfast, the Saja Boys Breakfast Meal includes a McDonald’s hash brown and a small soft drink, along with one other limited-time menu item:Spicy Saja McMuffin — a Sausage McMuffin with egg topped with a new Spicy Saja Sauce.The Derpy McFlurryJoining the March 31 lineup, there’s also a sweet middle-ground option. This new McFlurry is inspired by Derpy, the tiger character in the film, and is made with McDonald’s vanilla soft serve, berry popping pearls and a wild berry sauce.”Abigail Flores-Johnson covers food, beer and entertainment for the Coloradoan. You can reach her by email at abigailflores-johnson@coloradoan.com.
